title: Tenant overspill causes synchronous fallback and throttled bursts during regional surge
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: During a multi-region traffic spike for three large customers, several tenants experienced elevated 5xxs and throttled burst allocations. The autoscaler and admission controller allowed an overspill pattern where tenant burst tokens were synchronously routed to a fallback path (slower warm coldpool) causing headroom exhaustion and queue amplification. Customers reported degraded latency and denied bursts for sustained short windows, triggering escalations. This ticket tracks investigation, hotfix, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate multi-tenant surge: 20k rps distributed across 200 tenants with 5 tenants receiving 30% of the load each
Configure dedicated reserved pool with conservative headroom (10%) and burst_limit=300 tokens/min
Introduce transient KV cache eviction on a subset of replicas to trigger lease reallocation
Observe autoscaler and admission metrics: if admission controller returns synchronous fallback True, queues backpressure and burst denials occur
telemetry_summary: Spike correlated with 02:17 UTC regional surge. Headroom gauge dropped from 18% to 3% within 90s. AdmissionController.sync_fallback_count rose by 6x. Tenant burst_denied_rate spiked for top customers from 0.2% to 18%. Latency p95 for fallback path jumped from 120ms to 820ms. Autoscaler scale_up events lagged by median 70s due to sensor smoothing and lease-table stamp skew.
timeline: 2025-02-14 02:12 UTC: First customer alert - elevated latencies in EU region
2025-02-14 02:16 UTC: SRE paged, preliminary mitigation applied: increased temporary burst_limit for affected tenants via feature flag
2025-02-14 02:20 UTC: Engineering oncall reproduced issue in staging and confirmed synchronous fallback path is the primary amplification vector
2025-02-15 10:00 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis formed (see hypotheses). Began patch to decouple fallback routing and add asynchronous admission gating

2025-02-17 21:30 UTC: Hotfix deployed to canary: async fallback + short-lived overcommit token allowed (20% for 30s). Observed p95 latency drop by ~55% and burst_denied_rate fall to 1.3% for canary tenants
2025-02-18 08:45 UTC: Rollout to EU production completed with monitoring and rollback guard
hypotheses: Lease-table miscount during transient KV eviction led autoscaler to underreport actual warm replicas -> headroom underestimation
Admission controller was implemented as synchronous fallback (blocking call) causing request servicing thread to wait for fallback allocation instead of queuing asynchronously
Burst token accounting had an all-or-nothing gating rule that denied bursts when a tenant's reserve dipped below a static threshold, amplifying short windows of contention
Sensor smoothing windows in autoscaler too long for this workload pattern, delaying scale-ups
root_cause: A combination of a synchronous fallback admission path and a conservative burst gating rule produced a positive feedback loop: when lease-table briefly undercounted warm replicas (caused by concurrent KV eviction and restart churn), the admission controller routed requests to a slower fallback path synchronously. Requests blocked waiting for fallback allocation, causing queue buildup, which consumed burst tokens and triggered more denials. Autoscaler smoothing delayed replenishment, so the system stayed in the degraded state for ~1-3 minutes for affected tenants.
fix_and_patch: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7481 - Make admission fallback asynchronous and add non-blocking request proxying
PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1123 - Shorten scale sensor smoothing window for high-variance workloads and add immediate-probe path
PR: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/56 - Implement ephemeral overcommit token bucket (20% for 30s) for tenant bursts to smooth transient contention
Hotfix release: runtime-1.22.1 rolled to EU, US-West, APAC with rollback guard via feature-flag 'async-fallback-enabled'
rollback_and_mitigation: Immediate mitigation during incident: flagged affected tenants with temporary burst_increase via control-plane (feature flag), which reduced customer pain while patch was prepared
Rollback guard: if p95 latency in fallback path increases by >10% after rollout, feature-flag automatically disables async-fallback and alerts SRE
Runbook step added: if admission_fallback_count > 1000/min and headroom < 5% for >2min, trigger emergency warmup scale and enable ephemeral overcommit flag
follow_ups: Add lease-table convergence metric and alert when lease delta >5% for >30s
Expand chaos test suite to introduce KV eviction and replica churn during load tests to catch synchronous fallback regressions
Revise burst policy: replace static threshold with adaptive floor informed by traffic variance and qps history
Product: notify affected customers with summary and updated SLA mitigation steps; create ticket for account team to follow up
Console: add per-tenant burst_denial heatmap to aid support triage
notes: Customer escalations: Account teams for AcmeHealth, Finnova, and BetaChat were engaged; we provided temporary credits and immediate mitigations
This failure mode is distinct from previous reserved-pool 'headroom oscillation' incidents because amplification came from blocking fallback rather than autoscaler oscillation alone
We observed the ephemeral overcommit does introduce a small risk of momentary over-allocation - bounded by 20% and 30s TTL; telemetry will watch for steady state increase in GPU utilization
postmortem_summary: Primary fix: decouple fallback routing from request processing and introduce a short-lived adaptive overcommit allowance for bursts. Short-term mitigation (feature-flagged) provided immediate relief to customers. Follow-ups include improved lease-table visibility, adaptive burst thresholds, and expanded chaos testing. No customer data was exposed; impact was availability and increased latency only. Complete postmortem will be published to Confluence after closure.
